sections.html:
Fargo is the Cass County seat, on the western bank of the Red River of the North in the flat Red River Valley. Across the river is Moorhead, Minnesota. That border matters for taxes: a Fargo house follows North Dakota rules and a Cass County bill, while a Moorhead house falls under Minnesota law and a different county.

The city has grown steadily, from 90,599 residents in 2000 to 105,549 in 2010 and 125,990 in 2020, with a 2024 estimate of 136,285. A fire in 1893 wiped out 31 downtown blocks, so homes near downtown can be a century old or more, and age shows up in what buyers ask about.

Flooding is Fargo's main natural hazard. The Red River's minor flood stage here is 18 feet, and major flooding starts at 30 feet. Crests reached 39.5 feet in 1997, a record 40.84 feet in 2009 and 37 feet in 2010. By 2012 the city had bought 700 houses in flood-prone areas, and residents sandbagged in 2009.

The FM Area Diversion is the big permanent project meant to protect the metro area. Construction began in 2017 with a target of 2027. If your home sits in a flood-prone part of town, say so early. Buyers will ask, and the price will reflect the answer.

Winters are the other everyday test of a Fargo house. Roof and attic insulation, furnace age and capacity, basement moisture, the sump pump and window and door seals are what inspectors look at first. A cash buyer prices these items in directly, so you skip the round of repair requests after an inspection.

The City of Fargo assessor values your home, and Cass County sends the bill and collects the money. The assessor appraises property as of February 1 each year and has no say over the rate.

Rates come out of the budgets of each taxing body. City and county commissioners and school and park board members decide what they need, and the mill levy is that amount divided by total taxable value. Real estate statements go out in early December to the owner of record as of November 1, with a copy to your mortgage company.

Payments go to the Cass County Finance Office at 211 9th Street South in Fargo. You can also mail them, use the secure drop box or pay online. For property tax questions, call (701) 241-5600.

You can pay the full bill by February 15 for a 5 percent discount, or split it into installments due March 1 and October 15. Special assessments and drain taxes travel with the first installment and get no discount.

DateWhat happens
February 15Last day to pay in full and take the 5% discount
March 1First installment and specials due
After March 13% penalty on first installment
After May 16% total
After July 19% total
After October 1512% total on the first installment; 6% on the second

A deadline on a weekend or county holiday moves to the next business day, and a mailed payment counts if it is postmarked in time. Older delinquent real estate tax also picks up interest of 1 percent per month on the county's schedule.

The penalties come from North Dakota Century Code section 57-20-01 and the discount from section 57-20-09. A statement that never arrives does not stretch the discount date.

A special assessment pays for infrastructure that benefits particular parcels. A drain tax funds water or drainage work for particular parcels. Both are printed on the county statement, and neither earns the 5 percent discount.

Cass County lets you pay off a special assessment at any time. Until you do, a yearly installment is billed. Some drain taxes are one-time balances and others are ongoing maintenance charges.

Before you list, ask the title company to pull every remaining special and drain balance. Buyers and lenders will want either the payoff or a clear statement of who carries it after closing.

sections.h2: Credits and exemptions that may apply
sections.html:
Several state and city programs trim a Fargo bill, and they depend on the owner rather than the buyer. The Cass County page lists the main ones:

  • Primary Residence Credit, up to $500 against 2024 taxes, applied for through the State Tax Commissioner
  • Homestead Credit for owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled
  • Disabled veteran credit for a service-connected disability of 50 percent or more
  • Two-year new construction abatement that can cut taxable true and full value by $150,000

The City of Fargo adds a five-year exemption on value created by remodeling buildings that are 25 years old or older. If you finished a renovation before listing, that work may sit outside the tax base for a while, so mention it to the buyer.

Start with the Fargo assessor, then follow the board of equalization steps, which run in the same order every year. Local boards get the first 15 days of April, county boards the first 10 days of June, and the State Board of Equalization the second Tuesday in August.

  • The state board can lower a value only if you appealed to both the local and county boards.
  • Each owner gets a written notice showing true and full value for the current and previous year.
  • If the boards leave the problem unsolved, you can apply for abatement by November 1 of the year after the tax becomes payable.

Bring evidence: comparable sales, an appraisal or repair estimates. The assessor works by mass appraisal, so condition problems the office cannot see from the street are your strongest argument.

sections.h2: Selling a Fargo house with tax due
sections.html:
You can sell a Fargo house that has tax owing. The unpaid amount is normally settled from the sale proceeds at closing, and Cass County requires current-year taxes to be paid in full before a deed can be recorded.

The title company reads the county's figures, adds any special assessments, and pays the county from your proceeds. North Dakota charges no deed or mortgage tax, so recording costs are fees rather than a transfer tax.

Waiting costs money. Statements of Taxes Owing go out in March, May, July and October, and Notices of Tax Lien go out in November. Each May, certified Notices of Foreclosure of Tax Lien go to parcels with three years of unpaid taxes.

If the debt is old, a quick sale can protect your equity. We can review the county balance with you and make a written offer on the house as it stands, with no repairs and no commissions.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Fargo?
faqs.a: Cass County does. The City of Fargo Assessment Department sets the value, and the county Finance Office sends statements and takes payments at 211 9th Street South.

faqs.q: When is Fargo property tax due?
faqs.a: Pay in two installments on March 1 and October 15, or in full by February 15 for a 5 percent discount. Penalties start after March 1 on the first installment.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Fargo house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are paid from the proceeds at closing, and Cass County requires current-year taxes to be paid before a deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does North Dakota have a deed transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The state has no deed or mortgage tax, though recording fees still apply.

faqs.q: What happens if Fargo taxes stay unpaid for three years?
faqs.a: The county can begin tax lien foreclosure. Certified foreclosure notices go out each May for parcels three years behind, and the owner can still pay up to October 1.
